title: Types of water and weather hazards
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:45Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-makes-natural-hazard, is mainly about what turns an event into a hazard, and only touches the hydrological and atmospheric split, so it is broader than the new point and no bank point teaches this classification on its own.

draft.title: Types of water and weather hazards
card: A hazard is a natural event that can harm people, property or the environment. Hazards are grouped by what causes them.
These hazards involve water on or over the land. A flood is the main example: water covers land that is usually dry.
These hazards come from the weather. Examples are cyclones, severe storms, droughts and heatwaves.
A drought is a long period of much lower rainfall than usual. It is atmospheric because the weather causes it, even though it leaves water supplies short.
draft.remember: Hydrological hazards involve water. Atmospheric hazards come from the weather.

a.q: Which of these is an atmospheric hazard?
opts: A flood on the Hawkesbury River
Water covering a paddock near Lismore
A river bursting its banks at Wagga Wagga
a.why: A heatwave is a spell of very hot weather, so it is atmospheric. The other three are floods, where water covers land that is usually dry, which makes them hydrological.
a.clue: Which one comes from the weather rather than from water covering land?

b.q: Rain has barely fallen on a farming district near Dubbo for two years. Dams are low and crops are failing. How is this hazard best described?
opts: Atmospheric, because the weather causes it
Hydrological, because it affects water supplies
Hydrological, because water is missing from the land
Atmospheric, because it is a very strong windstorm
b.why: A drought is caused by a long spell of low rainfall, which is weather, so it is atmospheric. It is tempting to call it hydrological because the effects show up in dams and water supplies, but the card sorts hazards by their cause.
b.clue: Sort the hazard by what causes it, not by what it affects.

b.best: Atmospheric, because the weather causes it
